To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ISPs are motivated to deploy super-peering points because of the benefits to their customers; (2) content providers are motivated to deploy content caches at super-peer locations because it improves the search performance for their customers; and (3) topic-based search optimization can be deployed to significantly improve the search performance of super-peers with very modest storage overhead and minimal communication overhead.
(1) super-peers can be deployed by ISPs, content providers, or end-users and that (2) topic-based search optimization can be used to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of super-peers.

(a) service providers have a strong incentive to deploy super-peer servers in peer-to-peer networks, (b) the deployment of such servers can be optimized to provide better search performance to the end user, and (c) the optimization can be done without requiring significant additional storage or bandwidth at the super-peer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the incentives for service providers to participate in peer-to-peer networks, and with developing mechanisms to improve the performance of super-peer based peer-to-peer systems.
how to improve the performance of peer-to-peer networks by deploying super-peers and how to motivate the deployment of super-peers in the first place.

we propose the idea of topic-based search optimization and we show that it can significantly improve the performance of a super peer, and that the super peer itself has a very modest overhead in order to provide this service.
we propose a novel technical solution to a long-standing problem of P2P systems: super-peers are a solution in search of a problem.

The main takeaway from our work is that
super-peers can be an effective way of increasing the performance of peer-to-peer networks without the need for a centralized infrastructure or the cooperation of all peers.
, in a well designed peer-to-peer system, super-peers can be deployed by a service provider to improve search performance for its users without compromising the privacy of its clients.
, while super-peers may be more efficient than normal peers, they are not necessarily more efficient than a dedicated search engine.
